research_updates.title: Campus boundary and chronology resolved
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: IM3 campus inventory, Google location and opening pages, NC Commerce expansion history, City/County Project Cardinal records, air permits, contractor records, and exact 708 Lynhaven Drive/LNR4A/Project Cardinal queries. The selected object is the Google-operated Lenoir campus at 708 Lynhaven Drive, including multiple buildings and later adjacent expansion parcels; it is not a single building, the off-site solar plant, Google's Durham office, or the statewide portfolio. Google opened the first data center in May 2008 after the 2007 announcement; a second building served traffic by 2013, and later public records document LNR4A and Project Cardinal expansion work.

research_updates.title: City abatement audit resolves seven realized annual amounts
research_updates.notes: City ACFR GASB 77 notes were checked for FY2017-2025 through the Finance archive, direct archive-item URLs, and North Carolina Treasurer LG Reports. research_updates.title: Incentive, water-agreement, bond and compliance search
research_updates.notes: Official sources checked: October 22, 2024 joint agenda and minutes; City and County agenda archives; budgets, audits and capital schedules; NC Commerce JDIG and grant-report routes; NC legislative sales-tax statutes; exact Project Cardinal, Tapaha, Google, economic development agreement, clawback, annual grant, bond, debt, compliance and $6,880,000 searches. The executed agreement requires at least $600 million and 30 full-time jobs within five years and offers 20 annual grants equal to 50% of real-property and 85% of equipment/personal-property taxes, subject to reductions and clawback. No Project Cardinal grant has yet been observed. The water agreement fixes a $6,880,000 reserve fee and prevailing bulk rates, but no receipt, meter, invoice, payment, or consumption schedule was found.

research_updates.title: Air, environmental and compliance record audit
research_updates.notes: NC DEQ/EPA air-permit review and issued permit were checked for Facility ID 1400204, application 1400204.24A, permit 09733T10, renewal 1400204.25A, 708 Lynhaven, generators, Title V, PSD, emissions, inspection and enforcement terms. The permit resolves 163 authorized emergency generators. research_updates.title: Water, sewer, electricity and utility audit
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: Google 2024 impact and 2025 environmental reports; City public-utilities reports, water/wastewater budgets and rates; the 2017 and 2024 water-allocation agreements; Duke Energy Green Source Rider materials and NCUC orders; NC DEQ/EPA water and air routes. The 2024 report supplies 351.7 million gallons withdrawn, 23.9 million gallons discharged and 327.8 million gallons consumed at Lenoir; the impact study supplies 320.5 million gallons consumed in 2022 and 336.8 million in 2023. Only withdrawal has an adopted direct metric. No customer meter, bill, tariff determinants, annual kWh, campus MW load, sewer bill, peak demand, interconnection cost or public-utility capital allocation was found. Off-site 61 MW solar is not campus consumption.

research_updates.title: Workforce, payroll, procurement and training audit
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: original announcement coverage, NC Commerce, Google Careers and STAR program pages, NC Works/Commerce incentive and compliance routes, Caldwell County principal-employer tables, Caldwell Community College, Caldwell County Schools recipient pages, contractor records and exact jobs/payroll/wage/residence/training/procurement terms. The original 210-job and $48,300 average-salary plans and Project Cardinal's 30-job threshold are retained only as source projections. No realized annual-average FTE, Google payroll, benefits, contractor headcount, employee residence, occupation distribution, local hiring result, supplier transfer, or procurement ledger was found. A deterministic projected payroll scale is eligible; actual payroll and supplier models are rejected.

research_updates.notes: Operator, City, County, Caldwell Schools, Lenoir Housing Authority testimony, CISCC, CCC&TI, NCSSM and other recipient routes were checked for 2008-2026. research_updates.title: County outcome and public-cost candidate audit
research_updates.notes: BLS QCEW and BEA county panels, Census population context, City/County budgets and ACFRs, development records and service departments were reviewed over 2001-2025. A 2008 opening anchor permits descriptive matched-county employment and wage comparisons using 2001-2007 pretrends and 2024 outcomes. The analogous GDP result is rejected because the national matched estimate is -21.579900% while the North Carolina-only sensitivity is +4.719512%, a sign reversal. Employment and wage comparisons remain explicitly noncausal. No same-scope marginal police, fire, EMS, roads, water or administrative cost attributable to the campus was found, so no net fiscal or equal-cost threshold is asserted.

research_updates.title: Residual-gap model dispositions after candidate review
research_updates.notes: Retain twelve exact same-year Google-plus-Tapaha assessed-value aggregations; retain an exact 2007 projected annual payroll product; retain three water-consumption carry-through estimates with source-rounding bands; retain descriptive matched-county employment and wage comparisons with national K3/K5/K10, North Carolina K5 and leave-one-out sensitivity. Reject supplier/local-purchase and construction payroll models because no paid eligible base or geography exists; reject electricity-use/cost because PUE and solar capacity are not load; reject tax-receipt, net-fiscal and public-cost break-even models because gross project receipts, recipient distributions and same-scope marginal costs are absent; reject the GDP comparison for sign instability; reject Deloitte's statewide IMPLAN effects as already-modeled wider-scope outputs; and reject social-return scaling as directional and program-specific.

research_updates.title: Independent acceptance audit after adversarial continuation
research_updates.notes: accepted_after_adversarial_review. The post-candidate search re-ran exact Lenoir/Google/Tapaha/JDIG/jobs/incentive queries against state legislative, Commerce, local-government and operator routes and found a primary state record omitted from the candidate: approximately 50 employees in December 2008 and withdrawal of a JDIG application whose 200-job, four-year condition could not be met. The correction adds the point-in-time employee actual, and central reconciliation promotes the unmet JDIG condition to a governed direct projection record while keeping it distinct from operator employment projections. The original $10.143 million payroll product remains a projection-only counterfactual explicitly contradicted as a realized 2008 workforce scale. Source identifiers, project anchors, source locators, basis labels, periods, units, overlap rules, 98 fragment records and all 15 retained model derivations were independently reconciled; remaining gaps are actual annual-average FTE/payroll, suppliers, electricity/load, complete taxes and incentives, same-scope public costs, and causal outcomes.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Two independent staffing-equivalent sensitivities translate facility-specific continuous NOC and security coverage statements into the FTE capacity needed to cover one simultaneous post; neither is an observed employee count, the functions are not summed, and employer, overlap, shift, absence, residence and payroll remain unknown. A separate opening-configuration electricity sensitivity annualizes the directly reported 1.215 MW usable UPS capacity across utilization and PUE scenarios while checking the source-reported 3,000 kVA service capacity under power-factor assumptions. It is a theoretical nameplate envelope, not metered use, a true-value bound or an economic contribution. No model is created from 530 tons of cooling because electrical demand would require unobserved COP, part-load, redundancy and operating-hour inputs, and no model is created from generator counts, unit ratings, runtime or fuel storage because emergency standby nameplates do not measure annual operation. prj_study_im3_building_00844371952: Thirty residual modeled syntheses remain after the Google Bridgeport evidence audit. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. The three low-confidence county benchmark comparisons were removed: even with fit-sensitivity envelopes and explicit non-causal labels, they do not materially improve decisions about this campus and remain vulnerable to concurrent Meta expansions, Apple's separate campus and unrelated county changes. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps are retained because the direct record does not identify causal county outcomes. Every estimate remains unallocated, non-audited, and outside direct-record totals. Tax counterfactuals are not bills, payments, tax avoided, realized abatement, net fiscal benefit, or all-jurisdiction liability; wage and construction results are transferred benchmarks rather than observed Google payroll; DMR flow is not consumption or utility-billed volume. Supplier retention, electricity use/cost, actual public-service cost, and causal county outcomes remain unsupported. prj_study_im3_campus_00675108684: Dedicated last-resort Boydton model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Retained syntheses are limited to exact arithmetic over cited compatible observations: a five-fiscal-year average of the operator-reported portfolio property-tax total, its explicitly conditional same-scope public-cost break-even identity, and annual sums of identified LVL/Herbert Fund 301 components. All remain unallocated, modeled rather than observed, and non-additive to their source totals. project_description: Google operates a multi-building data-center campus at 708 Lynhaven Drive in Lenoir, Caldwell County, with Tapaha Dynamics holding associated real property. Announced in 2007, the first data center opened in May 2008 and a second building was serving traffic by 2013. Public records document later campus expansion phases, including LNR4A construction and the adjacent Project Cardinal parcels, while off-site solar remains supporting infrastructure rather than part of the campus boundary.
